variant_type_and_mechanism.statement: Predicted consequence from the batch HGVS: NP_000220.1:p.(Tyr168Cys). The papers describe the disease as autosomal recessive and caused by loss of LCAT function; the review also notes an intermediate (co-dominant) biochemical phenotype in heterozygous carriers.

quotes.quote: LCAT deficiency is a rare autosomal recessive disease [4, 5].
Loss of LCAT function causes decreased maturation of HDL particles and increased HDL levels of unesterified cholesterol and phosphatidylcholine.

carriers of one mutant LCAT allele show an intermediate biochemical phenotype between homozygous carriers and controls, suggesting that the disease, which is reported as recessive, is indeed co-dominant for the biochemical phenotype.

concerns: The variant appears only in a summary row of a systematic review table (34256778) without a case description; data are second-hand from the cited case report.
Table row contradicts itself: sample size 1, phenotype count 'FED:2'.
A second LCAT variant (c.440C>T) is listed; zygosity and phase not reported.
REF 35 does not appear to match the reference list entry [35].
notes_for_panel: Australian woman with FED, listed with c.503A>G and c.440C>T (both exon 4), zygosity and phase not stated. The row is internally inconsistent: sample size 1 but phenotype 'FED:2'. REF 35 in the table; in the reference list [35] is a Korean frameshift paper while [37] is Contacos et al. 1996, 'A new molecular defect ... associated with fish eye disease', so the source should be checked.
